newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GIANTS FIRE HEAD COACH DAN REEVES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-GIANTS FIRE HEAD COACH DAN REEVES.

text.p: Two days after completing a disappointing 6-10 season, the New York Giants fired head coach Dan Reeves on Monday.
The announcement was made by Giants general manager George Young, with whom Reeves was often at odds over personnel decisions.

"We made a change, whatever happened is history," Young said. "I think the coaching staff worked very hard and I think the differences between me and the coach were overstated, but I just think it was time to go in a new direction.
"We will start the evaluation process for a new coach immediately."
The Giants closed out their season on Saturday with a 23-22 loss to the playoff-bound New England Patriots, marking the first time since 1980 that New York had posted consecutive losing seasons.
It was the first time that Reeves had been part of back-to-back losing seasons in his 31-year football career.
Reeves had one year remaining at $1.3 million on his original five-year contract. But he said earlier this week that he believed his coaching days with the Giants were coming to an end.

During the past two seasons Reeves had been openly critical of his lack of input concerning personnel decisions under Young and director of player personnel director Tom Boisture. He lost out in his struggle to gain greater power over personnel matters following a 5-11 season in 1995.
With 149 career wins Reeves had the most victories of any active NFL coach, posting a 149-113-1 record. But he was 32-34 in four years with the Giants.
Reeves was fired by Denver after 12 seasons with the Broncos. Despite taking the Broncos to three Super Bowls, his public feuding with star quarterback John Elway ultimately cost him his Denver job.

New York hired Reeves as head coach in January of 1993 and finished 11-5 in his first season. But Giants veteran star quarterback Phil Simms was cut for salary cap reasons before the start of the 1994 season and Reeves was never happy with replacement starter Dave Brown.

Reeves is one of four NFL coaching casualties in recent days. The New York Jets sent Rich Kotite packing following a woeful 1-15 season, the Rams (6-10) fired coach Rich Brooks on Sunday after just two seasons in St Louis, and the Atlanta Falcons fired June Jones on Monday.
